title: 36th Bienal de Sao Paulo makes German debut at Haus der Kulturen der Welt
summary: With the exhibition Not All Travellers Walk Roads—Of Humanity as Practice, the 36th Bienal de São Paulo comes to Haus der Kulturen der Welt (HKW) in Berlin. Taking place in Germany for the very first time, the Berlin edition of one of the oldest and most influential biennials unfolds as a distinct constellation of artistic positions, including newly conceived, readapted, and site-specific works. Departing from Conceição Evaristo’s poem ‘Da calma e do silêncio’ [Of calm and silence], in which she writes: ‘Not all travellers / walk roads / there are submerged worlds / that only the silence / of poetry penetrates’, the exhibition understands listening as one of the core tenets of the practice of humanity. Through such close attunement, it becomes possible to enter into relation—with other beings, with lands and waters, with the multigenerational lineages we carry within us—and foster spaces of coexistence and care. title: Victoria Miro opens Modernisms exhibition featuring new paintings by Adriana Varejão
summary: Victoria Miro opened Modernisms, an exhibition of new paintings by Adriana Varejão. This body of work is conceived in direct dialogue with the artist’s participation in the Brazilian Pavilion at the 61st International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia (until 22 November 2026). While the tile paintings presented in the pavilion draw inspiration from Baroque and religious tilework of the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, the paintings in Modernisms shift the investigation towards Brazil’s modern period. They represent a temporal leap: from colonial tilework to modernist tiles, and from a tradition inherited from Portugal to a visual language that Brazil reinvented and made its own. For more than three decades, Varejão’s research has primarily focused on the Portuguese tiles that arrived in Brazil during the colonial period. These images constitute a vast iconographic

title: Laumeier Sculpture Park commissions new Alison Saar sculpture for 50th anniversary
summary: Laumeier Sculpture Park announces Begin Again: Honey Chile’, 2026, a new sculpture commission with acclaimed artist Alison Saar. Begin Again, the curatorial theme for Laumeier’s 50th anniversary, includes a series of projects whereby each artist has been invited to revisit a past project that has since been decommissioned or no longer exists, challenging the notion of sculpture parks as static museums. Honey Chile’ debuts October 3, 2026, in conjunction with Ursula von Rydingsvard's recently installed Untitled, 1989 (cast 2026), and Art & Nature Day, inviting visitors of all ages to explore art, nature, and community through hands-on activities and creative play. A mixed-race artist of African American, European and Native American ancestry, many of Saar’s sculptural objects stand as potent totems and often explore spiritual traditions

title: Rare 1959 works on paper by Cy Twombly highlighted at Galerie Karsten Greve
summary: Galerie Karsten Greve presents an exhibition dedicated to one of the most decisive bodies of work in Cy Twombly's oeuvre: the Sperlonga Drawings, created in 1959. Bringing together a rare group of works on paper, the exhibition revisits the summer of 1959, when the artist, recently settled in Italy, stayed in the village of Sperlonga on the coast of Lazio. During this pivotal period, Twombly produced around thirty works that marked a major turning point in his artistic practice. Nestled between Rome and Naples, Sperlonga is an emblematic place that held a profound fascination for Twombly. The artist was especially captivated by its Mediterranean light, describing the sea as "white three-quarters of the time." This luminous whiteness of the dazzling sun and the lime-washed houses permeates his works. title: Xippas Paris presents debut French showcase of Leandro Erlich's Classroom installation
summary: Xippas gallery, in partnership with GALLERIA CONTINUA, is presenting, for the first time in France, Classroom, an installation by Argentinian artist Leandro Erlich, at the Xippas Paris space. Following his exhibition at the Grand Palais in Paris, Leandro Erlich takes over the gallery space with a selection of works, including several previously unseen pieces. The exhibition opens with a suspended house, uprooted from the ground: Pulled by the roots BOG. Our roots, our points of attachment — these could serve as the guiding thread of the exhibition, which continues with a series of works entitled Draft-Bazza: various models of typewriters covered with sand and cracked, displayed beneath glass domes as though they had only just been unearthed. Like fragile relics from another era, buried beneath the sand, they evoke a bygone time—the pre-digital era, when communication was slower

title: Gazelli Art House now represents the Lilly Fenichel Foundation
summary: Gazelli Art House announced its representation of the Lilly Fenichel Foundation, formalising a relationship developed over several years and marking a new chapter in the international recognition of Austrian-born American artist Lilly Fenichel (1927–2016). The representation comes at a pivotal moment in the reassessment of Fenichel’s place within post-war American abstraction. Over a career spanning seven decades, she moved between some of its most significant artistic centres — San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles, and New Mexico — while maintaining an uncompromising independence from the movements and categories that surrounded her. Her work evolved continually, from the gestural language of her early paintings to geometric abstraction, sculpture, and experiments with unconventional materials, resisting any singular definition of her work. title: Greg Miller explores American pop culture and nostalgia in solo show at William Turner Gallery
summary: William Turner Gallery is presenting What’s Goin’ On, an exhibition of new paintings by Greg Miller. On view through November 7, 2026, the exhibition continues Miller’s decades-long exploration of American popular culture, memory, media, and the mythology of American life. For more than three decades, Miller has developed a distinctive visual language from the fragments of American culture —advertisements, comic books, magazine clippings, Hollywood imagery, signage, and other remnants of the American visual landscape. Combining found materials with painting, photorealism, gestural abstraction, and collage, he creates densely layered compositions in which images and text collide, overlap, and acquire new meanings. In What’s Goin’ On, Miller returns to the visual vocabulary of postwar America with a renewed sense of immediacy. Familiar images are extracted from their original contexts and

title: GR gallery presents first US solo exhibition by Japanese artist Kosuke Ajiro
summary: GR gallery is presenting Excavation Record I – Sayonara, the first solo exhibition in the United States by Japanese artist Kosuke Ajiro. The exhibition introduces Ajiro’s distinctive practice through the figure of the archeologist, who ventures into a whimsical and enigmatic imagined realm known as the “Kingdom of Sally.” Across the exhibition, each work reveals a fragment of this mysterious world, uncovering earthbound creatures and curious details before opening onto a vast, fantastical expanse. Moving between the familiar and the otherworldly, Ajiro’s works invite the viewer on a journey of mystery, magic, transformation, and discovery. As the story gradually reveals itself, viewers are invited to witness the rise and fall of the ‘Kingdom of Sally’ and participate in piecing together the discovered fragments that will one day rest in a temple dedicated to the art of storytelling. title: Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art opens decade survey of Samuel Levi Jones
summary: The Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art opened the exhibition, Samuel Levi Jones: An Archaeology of Knowledge, from September 12, 2026–February 14, 2027. In this exhibition, Jones investigates the underlying structures that shape how we see, speak, and think about culture, politics, and power. Borrowing its title from the ideas of the influential French philosopher Michel Foucault, Samuel Levi Jones: An Archaeology of Knowledge is built from ten years of Jones’s groundbreaking work in mixed-media painting and sculpture. While visiting the museum to develop the exhibition, Jones researched the museum’s collection to find works that resonate with the themes he interrogates, including nationalism and patriotism, censorship, and the representation of marginalized identities in historical narratives. title: Schick Art Gallery at Skidmore College presents 'Interrupting the After Image'
summary: Schick Art Gallery at Skidmore College presents “Interrupting the After Image,” an exhibition curated by Boryana Rusenova-Ina that brings together three artists — Ayesha Kamal Khan, Rusenova-Ina, and Choey Eun Young Cho — whose work draws from materials embedded in their everyday lives. On view from Sept. 10 through Oct. 8, “Interrupting the After Image” approaches questions of place, translation, distance, and memory from three distinct entry points. The artists investigate shifts in meaning that arise through geographic, linguistic, and material changes, articulating both those transformations and the ongoing evolution of what is encountered and what is remembered. An opening reception will be held from 5 to 6:30 p.m. Wednesday, Sept. 16, at Schick Art Gallery. title: Group exhibition at BredaPhoto Festival examines resistance and queer ancestors
summary: FOTODOK presents the group exhibition A Spell Bundle – Manifesting Queer Futurity at Clublokaal as part of the 12th edition of BredaPhoto Festival from 11 September until 25 October 2026. Inspired by the influential publication Cruising Utopia: The Then and There of Queer Futurity (2009) by José Esteban Muñoz, the project reflects on the idea of queer futurity: the tangible possibility of imagining and shaping a more just, inclusive, and joyful world beyond the limitations of the present. In the context of increasingly fascist and anti-queer rhetoric, this act of imagining becomes an essential form of resistance and world-building. A Spell Bundle – Manifesting Queer Futurity brings together works by artists Donja Nasseri, Ebun Sodipo, Julius Thissen, Nayara Leite, and S*an D. Henry-Smith. title: Bhutanese visual artist Pem Lham receives the 2026 Rubin Museum Himalayan Art Prize
summary: The Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art announced Bhutanese visual artist Pem Lham as the winner of the 2026 Rubin Museum Himalayan Art Prize, a $30,000 unrestricted cash prize and the largest international award in support of contemporary art related to Himalayan regions. Pem Lham accepted the award today at a celebration hosted by the Rubin in collaboration with the artist collective VAST Bhutan in Thimphu, Bhutan, where Pem Lham is based. “I have followed the Rubin Museum’s work in celebrating Himalayan art for many years, and receiving this recognition feels truly meaningful and beyond what I ever imagined,” says Pem Lham. “As artists, there are moments when we wonder if our stories are reaching anyone, but this prize is a reminder that our voices matter and that there are always people connecting with the work we create. title: Casino Luxembourg at the 16th Gwangju Biennale presents The Day of the Mantis
summary: Casino Luxembourg – Forum d’art contemporain presents The Day of the Mantis, an immersive film installation by Luxembourgish-German artist duo M+M (Marc Weis, Martin De Mattia) as part of the 16th Gwangju Biennale, You Must Change Your Life. Bringing together three films—Mad Mieter (2019), Club Bunker (2023), and the newly produced Silent Odd (2026)—the installation transforms the exhibition space into a fragmented cinematic environment inhabited by praying mantises and stick insects. Moving through three stereoscopic macro-film installations, visitors encounter non-human protagonists inhabiting spaces traditionally associated with human activity: apartments, bunkers, clubs and spaceships. Shot with a 3D macro camera and viewed through 3D glasses, the films create an unsettling sense of physical proximity, placing the viewer at eye level with the insects. title: Morris Museum challenges stereotypes of New Jersey life through contemporary photography exhibition
summary: In a forthcoming major exhibition project, candid photography—unscripted, unposed images taken from everyday life—by eleven contemporary artists explore the lives lived in the nation’s most densely populated and ethnically diverse state. Garden State Lens (opens October 16, 2026) presents scenes of New Jerseans going about their everyday lives. We see them raise their families, earn a living, come together as a community, and enjoy the state’s great outdoors. Powerful images—some printed at titanic scale, others more modestly sized—upend the typecast idea of our state through popular television shows and social media. title: Art Jameel presents its autumn 2026 programme
summary: Art Jameel, an organisation that supports artists and creative communities, presents ten exhibitions and commissions across Jameel Arts Centre in Dubai and Hayy Jameel in Jeddah, bringing together more than 65 artists and collectives across 20 geographies, spanning West, South and East Asia, the Gulf, the Red Sea and East Africa. Moving between painting, sculpture, drawing, installation, archival material, sound and living ecologies, the programme ranges from solo presentations and Art Jameel Collection-led exhibitions to expansive group shows and a new long-term garden commission. Drawn largely from the Art Jameel Collection, ‘Artists’ Rooms’ is a series of solo exhibitions by influential, innovative artists, with a particular focus on practitioners from West and South Asia. title: SculptureCenter selects six artists for In Practice 2027 Open Call series
summary: SculptureCenter announced the artists selected through our In Practice 2027 Open Call for Artist Proposals: Jianxin Tian, Thomas Tait, Anastasia Sosunova, Ash Moniz, Max Popov, and Jessica Wilson. Often combining mythological or whimsical motifs with elements of industrial design, Jianxin Tian hammers reliefs onto mass-produced metal objects, as if enchanting the mundane world. Tian presses and chisels sensual bodily forms onto domestic objects, continuing an initial motivation to draw out a poetics of kitchenware that formed during the pandemic lockdown. His practice, grounded in his training in Greco-Roman classical and modernist sculpture, is propelled by an urge to contend with the iconography of everyday life. title: Lucy Williams debuts architectural mixed-media collages at Miles McEnery Gallery
summary: Miles McEnery Gallery is presenting Lucy Williams’ inaugural solo show with the gallery. Williams’ intricate architectural mixed-media collages teeter between realism and abstraction. Heavily inspired by the British modernist movement and Bauhaus architecture,Williams’ scenes build worlds of splendid color, varied textures and an atmospheric sense of light. Each component is carefully conceived, with intentionally sourced materials that allude to historic references, female artist peers, and most recently, to previous works of her own.Williams shared that the works are “speaking to one another.” Williams’ process is thoughtful; consisting of color studies, woven textile tests, and color aid swatches. title: Andrew Jackson's Hermitage opens new satellite location in Marathon Village
summary: The Andrew Jackson Foundation, which owns and operates historic site and presidential home The Hermitage, announced today that its new satellite location, Andrew Jackson’s Hermitage Tickets and Tours, is now open in Marathon Village. Designed to educate, engage, and encourage curiosity about history, Andrew Jackson’s Hermitage Tickets and Tours will augment the work of the original Hermitage by providing another window into the historic landmark and the people who lived and were enslaved there. The store is designed around various questions that invite introspection and thoughtful engagement. title: David Peter Francis hosts first US solo exhibition by French artist Unglee
summary: David Peter Francis is presenting Le souvenir du temps, a solo exhibition by the French artist Unglee—his first in the United States. This much is true: Unglee makes photographs. Unglee makes films. Unglee first became known for his experimental films. Unglee’s experimental films oftentimes took the tulip as subject. Unglee cultivated countless varieties of tulips. Unglee loves tulips. According to an obiturary, Unglee was born in 1918. Unglee must be currently 108 years old. In this obituary, Unglee is survived by his ex-wife Arleen and son. Unglee has published multiple obituaries. Unglee likes to do things more than once. Unglee has died at least four times. Unglee had two wives. Unglee had an affair. Unglee loves drama. Unglee produced radio-dramas, broadcasted over France Culture radio. Unglee conducted interventions within the press.

title: LAUNCH LA presents group exhibition featuring four Los Angeles artists
summary: LAUNCH LA is presenting recent works by Los Angeles based artists Delbar Azari, Richard Bruland, Courtney Colgan and Lori Nielson who handle materials and manipulate surfaces in unique and captivating ways. These paintings and mixed media works defy simple categorization and yield impressive examples of technical precision and inspiring beauty. Delbar Azari is a former electrical engineer whose art practice explores how light, color, and material shape perception and space. Years investigating the balance between the industrial and the organic reveal how reflective and translucent materials can evoke calm, stillness, and quiet movement. title: Scottsdale Museum of Contemporary Art (SMoCA) presents Desert Perspectives, a year-long exhibition that uses the museum'
summary: Scottsdale Museum of Contemporary Art (SMoCA) presents Desert Perspectives, a year-long exhibition that uses the museum's collection as a living archive to examine how artistic representations of the greater Southwestern deserts evolve understandings of landscape, ecology, identity, and place. Bringing together works from the collection alongside contemporary commissions and loans, the exhibition traces more than a century of artistic engagement with these spaces, while proposing an alternative model for collection-based exhibition-making rooted in recontextualization, dialogue, and sustained inquiry. title: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea explores conceptual practices across Asia
summary: The conceptual turn in art, marked by a shift away from an emphasis on materiality toward the importance of ideas, has become a defining condition of contemporary art. This conceptual turn reopened the very question of what art was, expanding its meaning into new artistic and social dimensions. . The conceptual turn functioned as a major shift that opened up contemporary art, redefining what art is and offering a compelling artistic mode of engaging with society. The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea (MMCA) international symposium Art and Concept: In the Asian Context, held on August 19, 2026, presented a multifaceted discussion of the notion of "concept" within the contexts of Korea, Japan, and China.
